newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Firm Irish bonds seen steady in short term.
newsitem.headline: Firm Irish bonds seen steady in short term.

text.p: Irish bonds were marginally up on the day, dealers said on Monday, and were expected to remain steady in the near term.
Turnover meanwhile remained low, dealers said, inhibited by continuing concerns over the timetable for EMU.
"People are not increasing their weightings in non-core markets," a dealer said. "On the contrary they're pegging back on these markets to get back into bunds and we're being affected by that."

Further speculation on an EMU delay was fuelled by weekend press comments by a leading German economist who argued that Bonn would in all likelihood miss the tough entry rules on budget deficits and debt.

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was up 8.5 pence from Friday's close to 102.03 to yield 5.97 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 rose 12 pence from the close to 109.62 to yield 6.59 percent.

Dealers said activity would be capped by supply factors ahead of next Tuesday's auction by Ireland's National Treasury Management Agency of 150 million Irish pounds of the eight percent bond due 2006 on March 18.

The dealer said Irish paper was buoyed by robust UK gilts which got off to a strong start after Bank of England Governor Eddie George said underlying inflation would fall to the government's target of 2.5 percent this year.

Speaking to reporters at the Bank for International Settlements in Basle, Switzerland, he questioned whether it could stay there, but most market participants took that as the final nail in the coffin of a pre-election rate rise.
